a11y.audit_flow: Candidate audio and an authorized auditor are combined with access to an audited music diffusion model to produce a statistical membership evidence score.
a11y.manifold_alt: Conceptual two-dimensional projection of a learned generative support region, with member and non-member candidates shown on the same support but with different empirical local stability radii.
agent.copy: Behavioral probes may also help diagnose safety failures in agents by comparing responses under matched interventions. This is a research direction outside the music audit experiments.
baseline.endpoint.body: Compare the recovered endpoint with the clean input. A located journal baseline uses single-step predicted-clean latent MSE. A full reverse rollout defines a different comparison.
baseline.endpoint.title: Endpoint Reconstruction
baseline.equiv: At fixed t with the same noise and ε parameterization, single-step clean-sample MSE equals noise-prediction MSE scaled by (1 − ᾱₜ) / ᾱₜ. They can carry the same evidence.
baseline.intro: Add noise to a candidate and start denoising from the constructed state. Models may recover familiar training data more easily. Musical complexity, timbre, timesteps and noise draws also affect errors.
baseline.loss.body: Compare predicted noise with the injected ε. The located AudioLDM baseline code includes a normalized error norm and MSE variants. Its configuration uses six timestep ratios from 0.10 to 0.80, three seeded draws per ratio and a fixed “music” prompt at guidance scale 1.0.
baseline.loss.title: Diffusion Loss
baseline.other.body: Likelihood Ratio contrasts target and reference denoising evidence. Terminal Denoising Error measures error near the clean end. Embedding NN uses proximity in an embedding space. Lower errors are oriented toward higher membership evidence.
baseline.other.title: Other baseline signals
baseline.secmi.body: A music adaptation of step-wise error, comparing a local deterministic forward/return estimate with its reference state.
baseline.secmi.title: SecMI-style posterior error
baseline.space: These equations illustrate waveform diffusion and endpoint error. Latent diffusion applies the noise and reverse steps in z-space. A latent MSE compares internal tensors. A waveform comparison requires decoding.
chn.boundary: A positive residual places a candidate above its local quantile. The final decision uses a separate 1% calibration. MS-CHN addresses similarity-related score variation. The role of augmentation remains a mechanism hypothesis.
chn.common.body: If similar non-members also score high, the candidate’s stability is less unusual.
chn.common.title: Stable candidate, stable neighbors
chn.excess.body: A candidate well above its neighbors retains stronger conditional excess evidence. Some non-members can still exceed their background.
chn.excess.title: Stability above the local background
chn.features: A located feature export has 512 CLAP and 93 acoustic columns (605 total). An earlier export reported 87 acoustic and 599 joint. The method draft describes L₂-normalized CLAP, reference-fitted robust acoustic scaling and concatenation. Historical code uses Euclidean neighbors. Final column selection, scaling and family weights await the aligned configuration.
chn.motivation: Random cropping gives a training track several possible views. Generalization can give unseen tracks with similar rhythm, harmony, timbre, production or style high stability too. A global comparison can count this shared response as evidence about a particular track. Naturally occurring musical similarity can produce the same problem.
chn.question: How much of high stability is evidence of training exposure, and how much is the response we would expect for similar music?
chn.scope: The score estimates excess stability relative to similar non-members. It cannot identify which crop was presented during training or reconstruct an unaugmented original.
chn.steps.1: Represent music with frozen CLAP and acoustic descriptors. Fit preprocessing on known reference non-members in C_ref.
chn.steps.2: Retrieve k nearest reference non-members. Similarity selects the comparison group.
chn.steps.3: Estimate the upper quantile of their Raw MS scores and subtract it from the candidate score. The draft uses k = 200 and q = 0.95.

lsa.boundary: The normalization scale, DDIM randomness, perceptual degradation threshold and final membership cutoff serve distinct purposes. The budget is a search approximation. Member stability is a hypothesis tested on these targets.
lsa.name: Latent Stability Adversarial Probe · ICASSP 2026
lsa.search.1: Scale the perturbation by the forward noise amplitude √(1 − ᾱₜ).
lsa.search.2: Inner projected gradient descent (PGD) searches for a direction that increases response change.
lsa.search.3: Outer bisection estimates the budget needed to cross a fixed perceptual degradation level. A larger budget provides more member-like evidence in the reported probe.
lsa.settings: Deterministic DDIM, timestep ratio 0.60, ℓ₂ budget up to 0.80, and CDPAM degradation. The paper reports 12 PGD steps, five restarts and ten bisection iterations. The matched-compute comparison uses per-sample wall-clock time on A100-80GB within 5%.
meta.description: LSA-Probe and MS-CHN study white-box membership auditing for music diffusion models.
meta.title: LSA-Probe / MS-CHN · Membership auditing for music diffusion
plate.1.alt: A candidate music file enters a target checkpoint in a white-box audit. Paired internal responses and reference non-members provide membership evidence.
plate.1.caption: The question is whether this checkpoint trained on the candidate track. Known non-members give its response a reference level.
plate.1.title: Was this music used for training?
plate.2.alt: One item ID spans a timeline with variable training windows and one fixed center audit window. The training manifest labels the track.
plate.2.caption: Membership follows the original track ID. A fixed query crop can carry the track’s label even when training sampled other windows.
plate.2.title: Training views and audit queries
plate.3.alt: The upper bracket compares the original latent z₀ with its reconstruction ẑ₀. The lower bracket compares unperturbed and perturbed denoising responses under the same model, conditioning and paired randomness.
plate.3.caption: Reconstruction compares ẑ₀ with the original latent z₀. Stability compares unperturbed and perturbed responses under paired randomness.
plate.3.title: Reconstruction and stability
plate.4.alt: Outer bisection sets η. Inner PGD projects δ to that budget. Paired perceptual degradation relative to τ updates the interval until C_adv is estimated.
plate.4.caption: To cross a fixed perceptual threshold, PGD searches for a direction and bisection estimates the required budget.
plate.4.title: LSA-Probe
plate.5.alt: Fixed-amplitude directions at several diffusion times yield paired response distances and sensitivities. Transform stability against reference non-members at each time and aggregate to S_MS.
plate.5.caption: At a fixed perturbation size, a smaller paired response change yields a higher stability coordinate.
plate.5.title: Raw Manifold Stability
plate.6.alt: Frozen features select similar reference non-members. Subtract their local Raw MS q95 from candidate Raw MS. Two conceptual examples place the candidate near or above this background.
plate.6.caption: Similarity selects the controls. A positive residual places the candidate above its neighbors’ upper quantile; a separately calibrated cutoff determines the decision.
plate.6.title: MS-CHN
plate.7.alt: C_ref fits the scoring map and local reference. With this map frozen, C_thr sets a cutoff. Held-out E₀ and E₁ measure FPR and TPR with the frozen rule.
plate.7.caption: Independent-reference manuscript protocol. Alignment with the original labels and scores behind the July results remains unresolved.
plate.7.title: Reference, calibration and evaluation
plate.8.alt: Conference baseline and LSA-Probe TPR pairs are 10/13, 8/14, 12/20 and 11/18 percent. July Raw MS and MS-CHN TPRs are 9.19% and 16.55%, with empirical FPRs of 0.56% and 0.70%.
plate.8.caption: Manuscript-reported. ICASSP Table 1 and the July AudioLDM draft use separate protocols. The July values use the earlier calibration pool; replay under the later independent protocol remains unresolved.
plate.8.title: Results by protocol
plate.baseline_note: The located AudioLDM endpoint baseline predicts a clean latent in one step and measures latent MSE.
plate.data_note: The July common-pool result and September independent-role design have distinct provenance.

protocol.design: The September design summary specifies five rotating non-member folds, with 5,000 reference tracks, 2,000 threshold-calibration tracks, 1,000 evaluation non-members and 500 evaluation members per target and fold. Choose configurations on M1/M3/M5 and D1/D3/D5; then evaluate on M2/M4/M6 and D2/D4/D6. Aggregate within target first and use independently trained targets as the units of cross-target variation.
protocol.e0.body: Held-out non-members measure the empirical false-positive rate.
protocol.e0.title: E₀ · Evaluation non-members
protocol.e1.body: Members held out of score fitting measure the true-positive rate, or member recall.
protocol.e1.title: E₁ · Evaluation members
protocol.intro: Fit the full scoring map before threshold calibration. In each target and fold, check role disjointness and ground truth using original track IDs.
protocol.rank: For the rank-calibrated rule, flag when p(x) ≤ 0.01. This rank measures score extremeness among calibration non-members. It does not estimate the probability that a query is a member. Empirical FPR can vary across finite batches and subgroups.
protocol.ref.body: Known non-members fit per-time score transforms and feature preprocessing, and populate the local score library. Exclude the query’s own track when scoring reference items.
protocol.ref.title: C_ref · Reference
protocol.thr.body: A separate set of known non-members calibrates the decision after the score mapping is frozen.
protocol.thr.title: C_thr · Threshold calibration
protocol.verify: Role manifests and aligned scores are needed to verify those sizes, disjointness, leave-one-out and near-duplicate rules. Earlier manuscript tables describe a shared calibration pool. Repeated tracks across folds do not create new independent observations.
raw.boundary: Raw MS extracts local-response evidence. Similar non-members can still have high raw scores.
raw.config: The draft specifies t/T ∈ {0.55, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70}, η = 0.001, eight directions and direction quantile 0.90. TSS4 names the four time coordinates. H = 2 is the number retained after reference rank transformation and Gaussianization. The inspected AudioLDM wrapper rolls back multiple DDIM steps and returns a latent. The inspected DiffWave pilot uses deterministic reverse steps in waveform space. Historical code sums the top two coordinates even when negative. The final positive-only rule and response implementation still require an aligned artifact.
raw.intro: The journal’s Raw Manifold Stability score probes with fixed-amplitude directions using forward computations. Its evidence comes from the response to a small neighborhood of the intermediate state.
raw.steps.1: At each selected time, divide the paired response distance by the perturbation norm for each seeded direction.
raw.steps.2: Take the negative high quantile of directional sensitivities. Greater sensitivity gives lower stability.
raw.steps.3: Transform time coordinates against reference non-members, then aggregate across time.

result.conf.intro: The conference reports gains of 3–8 percentage points at 1% FPR across its four comparisons. Best Baseline is the best of Loss, Trajectory and SecMI. The paper uses DeLong for AUC confidence intervals and sample bootstrap for TPR intervals.
result.conf.table.caption: Conference Table 1 · TPR (95% CI) / AUC ± 95% CI half-width
result.journal.pending: The September-only DiffWave main comparison, Embedding NN, acoustic-only ablation and paired top-bin lifts await source alignment.
result.journal.status: Draft-reported AudioLDM-style results. The located manuscript reports these values under its earlier calibration description. The original training labels and scores for the later independent-reference protocol have yet to be aligned to these tables. Treat the results as manuscript reports with unresolved replay provenance.
result.journal.summary: The draft reports member recall of 9.19% for Raw MS and 16.55% for MS-CHN, a gain of 7.36 percentage points under the same nominal 1% calibration target. Their measured FPRs are 0.56% and 0.70%, respectively.
result.limits: Similarity-conditioned scoring can leave uneven false-positive risk. An augmentation-on/off effect needs matched training runs. Results are specific to these datasets, model families and access assumptions.
result.rq.1: Do false positives concentrate? The earlier draft reports a 4.64× average top-bin lift for Raw MS in music-matched neighborhoods and 1.21× with random neighborhoods. Lift is top-bin FPR divided by overall FPR. Values above 1 indicate concentration.
result.rq.2: Does probing help? The draft reports AUC 0.6267 and 9.19% recall for Raw MS. These describe signal on its evaluated targets and operating point.
result.rq.3: Does matching help? The draft-reported joint feature row increases recall. The ablation and historical score replay differ in their label and calibration provenance, so the size of the gain awaits reconciliation.

task.access.body: Loss baselines and fixed-direction stability use forward queries and intermediate states. Conference LSA-Probe also backpropagates through the reverse computation. MS-CHN additionally requires music known to be absent from the target training set.
task.access.title: White-box access
task.boundary: Training manifests establish experimental labels and are withheld from the scorer. A positive decision is statistical evidence about the audited training stage. A legal finding requires separate evidence.
task.item.body: The journal training unit is an FMA track. A query uses a fixed crop. Every crop of one track shares its label for that target, even if the exact waveform was never seen. Its label can change with the checkpoint.
task.item.title: Membership is checkpoint-specific
task.lead: A membership inference attack (MIA) estimates whether a candidate training item belongs to the training set of a specified checkpoint. It provides statistical evidence for data provenance, privacy and model security audits.
training.conf.caption: Conference paper, §3
training.conf.row0.1: MAESTRO v3 and FMA-Large. Four-second training clips are members. Validation or test clips supply non-members.
training.conf.row1.1: 22.05 kHz training and 16 kHz scoring. The paper reports stratification by piece or track and artist, with Chromaprint and LSH duplicate and cover screening.
training.conf.row2.1: Waveform DDPM in the DiffWave family. The paper reports 200,000 steps, batch 32, AdamW and cosine learning-rate decay.
training.conf.row3.1: Unconditional diffusion in VAE latents. The decoder is frozen during auditing and the reported probe distances compare decoded waveforms.
training.intro: We train controlled targets with documented training sets so we can check membership against each checkpoint’s manifest. The journal labels concern the denoiser’s training stage. Pretrained components have their own training histories.
training.journal.caption: Located FMA-Large training records
training.journal.row0.1: Each of six AudioLDM-style targets has 95,916 training, 5,328 validation-pool and 5,330 test-pool tracks. The three source pools have zero track-ID overlap within each target. The inspected training runner builds its validation loader from the test pool. Audit folds are downstream.
training.journal.row1.1: Train with a random 10.24 s crop. The loader samples starts over the available range and retries quiet windows up to ten draws. Validation uses the center crop. The loader resamples to 16 kHz, uses the first channel, removes the mean and peak-normalizes to 0.5. It pads short usable clips with zeros. The training loader advances to the next track after an extraction exception. Manifest counts describe dataset inclusion.
training.journal.row2.1: Latent U-Net with ε prediction, a frozen pretrained KL autoencoder, its frozen pretrained HiFi-GAN vocoder, and frozen pretrained CLAP. Training conditions on manifest captions mapped to FiLM, with 0.10 classifier-free condition dropout. The mel input has 64 bands, a 1,024-sample FFT and window, and a 160-sample hop.
training.journal.row3.1: AdamW, learning rate 0.0001, 2,000-step warmup, configured batch size 2, and a 1,000-step diffusion schedule with linear schedule endpoints 0.0015 and 0.0195. The trainer selects by step count. The six weights contain EMA state and record global_step 800,000 internally; their inventory labels read 799,999.
training.journal.row4.1: One completed FMA run uses unconditional waveform diffusion, with 30 dilated residual layers, 64 residual channels and a dilation cycle of 10. Its config uses 16 kHz, 10.24 s crops, seed 0, batch 4, Adam at 0.0002 and 800,000 steps. The full six-target family remains unverified.
training.split: The journal design is track-based. Artists, albums and alternative recording versions can span roles.
training.types.1: Preprocessing sets sample rate, channel and amplitude conventions.
training.types.2: Training views vary the crop of one track. All six inspected AudioLDM configs set audio mixup to zero. Other augmentation switches lack aligned evidence.
training.types.3: Forward Gaussian noise is part of the diffusion process.
training.types.4: The audit adds a controlled perturbation δ to an intermediate state.
